title: fix: keep approved app PRs open through merge delays
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Updates the GitHub actions to Node 24-based releases while keeping app scripts on Node 22
- Retries a catalog merge once after the normal auto-merge window
- Leaves a healthy catalog PR open when GitHub auto-merge is delayed
- Prevents transient GitHub failures from sending approved apps back to review

gist.headline: The garden gate stays open
gist.blurb: Approved app submissions now get a little more patience from the hive. If GitHub lingers during auto-merge, the healthy catalog PR stays open instead of being sent back through review.
gist.summary: The app-publishing workflow now retries a delayed catalog merge once and keeps healthy approved catalog PRs open through transient GitHub auto-merge failures, while updating GitHub Actions to Node 24 and retaining Node 22 for app scripts.
gist.impact: App contributors will see approved submissions survive temporary GitHub merge delays instead of unnecessarily returning to review.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli as a careful garden keeper holding open a cozy lime-green garden gate for an approved app seedling, while a friendly CRT monitor robot watches a delayed merge timer settle into a green check mark. The open gate represents preserving an approved PR through GitHub's occasional hesitation, with code-plants and small catalog cards growing safely inside.
